core_job: For US buyers who are already touring homes: work out a lender-style monthly budget from their own figures (income, debts, deposit, rate; front-end and back-end DTI; principal, interest, tax, insurance, PMI and HOA), then measure every specific home they are considering against that budget. The budget engine already exists and works (lib/core/finance/affordability.dart:56-174). The weekly rate comes from FRED (Freddie Mac PMMS), keyless; I curled it today and got HTTP 200, latest row 2026-10-08,7.40.
signature: Offer Check: the user adds homes they are touring, typed in themselves (asking price plus, optionally, that home's own tax bill, HOA, insurance, link and notes). For each home the app shows: (1) the true monthly cost using that home's own tax and HOA; (2) a verdict: Fits / A stretch (up to 10% over) / Over budget; (3) a walk-away price, meaning the highest offer that keeps the user inside their DTI limits, solved by bisection on the same breakdownAt maths; (4) what it would take for a stretch or over-budget home: extra deposit, the rate needed (shown against this week's PMMS average), debt reduction, or price reduction; (5) monthly cost at -0.25% and +0.25% rate. Everything runs on the device with no account. It replaces the build-flag listings feed, which needed paid MLS data, with homes the user enters. Competitors checked only through their own App Store descriptions via the iTunes API: Mortgage Pal (calculators, no saved homes), CazaHQ (house tracker, no budget maths), RECalc, GetWyz. I could not run a web search because it is disabled here, and Zillow/Redfin are not verified.
